sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for the petitioners and learned HCGP for the respondent-State.
2. This petition is filed by the petitioners who are farmers by profession and owners of the land at Gulgaljamabagi village of Mudhol taluka, Bagalkote district.

The main occupation and source of income is dependent on farming,
agriculture and which is generated by growing commercial crops in their properties owned by them.

Unfortunately, the lands of the petitioners were submerged under the back water of Upper Krishna Project, due to which the petitioners are unable to cultivate their lands and now are rendered without land and unable to meet the daily needs.

Respondent No.4 issued a preliminary notification for acquisition under Section 11(1) of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (for short, 'the ACT, 2013') dated 03.09.2022 to acquire the lands of the petitioners and thereafter, a final notification came to be issued under Section 19(1) of the Act, 2013 dated 26.04.2023 for the purpose of Upper Krishna Project.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 3. Learned counsel for the petitioners contends that despite issuance of the preliminary notification and the final notification, no efforts are made to pay the compensation for the lands which belonged to the petitioners which are submerged for the project of Upper Krishna Project.

Therefore, due to the inaction of the respondents and high handedness,
illegality and arbitrariness, petitioners are before this court.
Now petitioners are knocking at this court for suitable relief.

4. It is the fundamental rule of law even the principles of natural justice warrant whenever the land of a citizen of this country is acquired and possession is taken, the compensation would have to be awarded by the State which is a 'parens patriae'.
But in the present case, admittedly the land has been acquired, final notification has been issued but no compensation has been paid.

So therefore,
there is a violation of Article 14 of the Constitution of India and also the principles of natural justice and the right to livelihood.

The State which is the guardian of the citizens, under such circumstances will have to initiate proper procedures in accordance with law and award compensation after acquisition by taking possession, to the citizens without delay and causing harassment to the citizens.

5. Per Contra, the learned HCGP representing the State, agrees with the notification being issued and the NC: 2024:KHC-D:7225 project being initiated and the petitioners land being taken to the particular project that is Upper Krishna project.
She contends that within a reasonable time the compensation would be awarded in accordance with law.

6. Placing the submission on record, the petition requires to be allowed, accordingly, this court proceeds to pass the following :
